task: T-212 / T-213 — finishing the two audits C-0129 measured, published, and declined to gate
leaf: none for T-212 (a process task); A8.2 for T-213, whose six files are all flatness studies
verificationType: logical (two static censuses over the committed corpus, before and after, each with a stated catch set and self-tested discriminators) + in-silico (35 studies re-run through one snapshot and diffed field by field against their COMMITTED version read out of git, with a control re-run wherever a non-departure field moved)
maturity: TRL 1-3, and below it: NO PHYSICS CHANGED. Every number this task moved is a diagnostic or a precision. Not one computed quantity moved.

units.note: nothing physical is computed. Units unchanged and untouched: nm, pN, pN/nm, pressure in pN/nm^2 = 1 MPa exactly, k_BT = 4.141947 pN nm at 300 K, aqueous buffer with stated Mg2+
units.departure: dimensionless — and that is part of the definition, which is what CH-0154 is about

cheapBounds.name: bound 1 — how many files does each audit still touch, and do the two sets OVERLAP?
cheapBounds.measured: 27 files owe a departure repair and 6 owe a saturated-proportion repair; three — T-155, T-162, T-191 — are in BOTH
cheapBounds.decided: the two are ONE re-emission sweep and not two. Run separately, each of the three overlapping files is re-run twice and the second diff has to be separated from the first; and two topological sorts over overlapping sets can put a consumer of one before a producer of the other (CH-0131).

cheapBounds.name: bound 2 — is the rule the map expresses the rule the claim states? (falsifier F4)
cheapBounds.measured: the leaf key `departure` appears under ELEVEN parents in gpd/results/. T-193's is a difference of two electrode potentials in VOLTS; T-160's `departures[*].relativeDeparture` is that study's own ANSWER, declared at six digits.
cheapBounds.decided: the mechanism is re-keyed on `record/spelling` rather than on the leaf name, and the alternative — making DEPARTURE_DIGITS_BY_KEY the default of roundedForResult, one line instead of 27 — is REFUSED on this measurement rather than on taste. It would have touched 66 files and rounded a literature comparison in volts to two digits.

cheapBounds.name: bound 3 — can the six files on the actuator rounding path obey the rule at all?
cheapBounds.measured: roundedForActuatorResult() takes NO ARGUMENTS. There is no digitsByKey to pass.
cheapBounds.decided: T-60 is one of C-0129's 27 and was not 'one re-run away': it was one re-run and a change to a rounding implementation in another package away. The delegation adds T-3, T-4, T-76, T-149 and T-157 to the sweep, and that obligation is explicit — changing a rounding implementation without re-emitting what it emits is the one thing CLAUDE.md forbids outright.

cheapBounds.name: bound 4 — how wide is the RULE against the GATE's predicate?
cheapBounds.measured: C-0129's strict predicate is the leaf key `departure` inside a reproductions or convergence record. The same records carry three more spellings of the same quantity: 564 `departure`, 503 `relativeDeparture`, 337 `departureFromFinest`, 12 `relativeDepartureInStroke`.
cheapBounds.decided: the gate is wired on C-0129's own predicate, where the tree can be made clean, and the wider scope is PRINTED BESIDE IT, ungated. A gate that reports a number it does not enforce is the honest form of C-0083; a gate that reports only what it enforces is how a narrow predicate becomes a claim of cleanliness.

cheapBounds.name: bound 5 — which of the 35 re-runs are cheap and which are heavy?
cheapBounds.measured: three studies were timed before anything was edited, spanning the classes: a closed-form lattice census, a two-dimensional field solve, and the largest Monte Carlo ensemble in the corpus. The spread is a factor of ~170.
cheapBounds.decided: the sweep is affordable, and it is run as ONE snapshot with 35 runs inside it rather than 35 snapshots (tools/study-batch.sh). No timing is emitted into this file — CLAUDE.md: a wall clock in a result file is a step counter by another name — so the cost is published as a COST CLASS and each study's own declared workload, which are deterministic.

departureAudit.rule: C-0093, C-0101: a departure — a difference or ratio of two nearly equal DIMENSIONLESS numbers, emitted inside a reproductions or convergence record — carries two significant digits, because RESULT_ABSOLUTE_FLOOR is a claim in the LOCKED UNITS and does not reach a ratio (P-18).
departureAudit.gatePredicate: the leaf key `departure` inside a reproductions or convergence record, at more than two significant digits — C-0129's own strict predicate, unchanged, so that the before/after numbers are comparable
departureAudit.ruleScopePredicate: any of the four spellings the corpus uses (departure, relativeDeparture, departureFromFinest, relativeDepartureInStroke) inside such a record — the rule, which is wider than the gate and is REPORTED rather than enforced
departureAudit.mechanism: DEPARTURE_RECORDS x DEPARTURE_SPELLINGS as `record/spelling` keys in structure/ResultRounding.kt, with most-specific-wins precedence in roundedForResult; and actuator/ActuatorResultRounding.kt delegating to it instead of hand-copying it
departureAudit.whyTheRecordQualifierIsLoadBearing: T-193 emits `potentialOfZeroCharge[*].departure` in VOLTS and T-160 emits its own answer as `departures[*].relativeDeparture` at six digits. A map keyed on the leaf name would round both. CH-0154.

saturationAudit.defect: at p-hat = 1 (or 0) the symmetric binomial standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/n) is IDENTICALLY ZERO for every n, so it cannot distinguish 1250 draws from 20000. A saturated statistic is the resolution of nothing.
saturationAudit.instrument: coupling.saturatedProportionBound — the exact one-sided Clopper-Pearson limit at x = n, p > (1 - c)^(1/n), whose large-n form is the rule of three
saturationAudit.whereTheRepairWENT: on the SHARED SUMMARY, coupling.DropoutDishing, which all seven studies build through summariseDropoutDishing — not at six emission sites. C-0129 repaired T-148 at its emission site, which is the same shape as the three per-file departure repairs its own section 3 diagnoses.
saturationAudit.aRecordIsREPAIREDNotRemoved: the symmetric error stays where the one-sided bound is emitted beside it. It is uninformative rather than wrong, and removing it would break every reader of the schema.
saturationAudit.theDegeneracyIsWhereTheAnswersAre: all seven affected files are studies whose headline is that a design FAILS T-5b's 0.10, which is exactly the direction that saturates the exceedance at 1.0. The better a design is, the more informative the symmetric error; the worse it is, the less. A statistic that goes blind in the direction of the finding is not a weak instrument, it is the wrong one.
